topics.title: Appendix E — Glossary
topics.summary: Arithmetic intensity — The amount of computation performed relative to data movement.

blocks.text: Arithmetic intensity — The amount of computation performed relative to data movement.

blocks.text: Backpressure — A bounded mechanism by which a downstream stage limits upstream production.
rich: — A bounded mechanism by which a downstream stage limits upstream production.

blocks.text: Coalescing — Combining memory activity from nearby GPU threads into efficient memory transactions when access patterns permit it.
rich: — Combining memory activity from nearby GPU threads into efficient memory transactions when access patterns permit it.

blocks.text: CPU reference implementation — A deliberately inspectable implementation used to define expected semantics independently of an optimized GPU path.
rich: — A deliberately inspectable implementation used to define expected semantics independently of an optimized GPU path.

blocks.text: Deadline — The time by which a unit of work must complete according to a stated requirement.
rich: — The time by which a unit of work must complete according to a stated requirement.

blocks.text: Device — In CUDA terminology, a GPU or other CUDA-capable execution target controlled by host code.
rich: — In CUDA terminology, a GPU or other CUDA-capable execution target controlled by host code.

blocks.text: Divergence — A condition in which threads executing together follow different control-flow paths, potentially reducing execution efficiency.
rich: — A condition in which threads executing together follow different control-flow paths, potentially reducing execution efficiency.

blocks.text: End-to-end latency — Elapsed time across the complete boundary relevant to the user or system contract, rather than one internal stage.
rich: — Elapsed time across the complete boundary relevant to the user or system contract, rather than one internal stage.

blocks.text: Heterogeneous computing — Computing that deliberately divides work among processors with different architectures or execution characteristics.
rich: — Computing that deliberately divides work among processors with different architectures or execution characteristics.

blocks.text: Occupancy — A CUDA resource and scheduling metric describing active warps relative to architectural limits; it is not a direct measure of useful throughput.
rich: — A CUDA resource and scheduling metric describing active warps relative to architectural limits; it is not a direct measure of useful throughput.

blocks.text: Pinned memory — Host memory arranged to support direct asynchronous transfer behavior required by particular CUDA workflows.
rich: — Host memory arranged to support direct asynchronous transfer behavior required by particular CUDA workflows.

blocks.text: Real-time system — A system whose correctness includes timing requirements in addition to logical results.
rich: — A system whose correctness includes timing requirements in addition to logical results.

blocks.text: SIMT — Single instruction, multiple threads; CUDA's execution model in which threads are grouped for hardware execution while retaining thread-level semantics.
rich: — Single instruction, multiple threads; CUDA's execution model in which threads are grouped for hardware execution while retaining thread-level semantics.

blocks.text: Stream — A CUDA ordering domain for asynchronous operations.
rich: — A CUDA ordering domain for asynchronous operations.

blocks.text: Throughput — Completed work per unit time under a stated workload.
rich: — Completed work per unit time under a stated workload.

blocks.text: Warp — The hardware execution grouping used by NVIDIA GPUs for CUDA threads.
rich: — The hardware execution grouping used by NVIDIA GPUs for CUDA threads.

reading.title: Appendix E — Glossary
paragraphs: Arithmetic intensity — The amount of computation performed relative to data movement.
Backpressure — A bounded mechanism by which a downstream stage limits upstream production.
Coalescing — Combining memory activity from nearby GPU threads into efficient memory transactions when access patterns permit it.
CPU reference implementation — A deliberately inspectable implementation used to define expected semantics independently of an optimized GPU path.
Deadline — The time by which a unit of work must complete according to a stated requirement.
Device — In CUDA terminology, a GPU or other CUDA-capable execution target controlled by host code.
Divergence — A condition in which threads executing together follow different control-flow paths, potentially reducing execution efficiency.
End-to-end latency — Elapsed time across the complete boundary relevant to the user or system contract, rather than one internal stage.
Heterogeneous computing — Computing that deliberately divides work among processors with different architectures or execution characteristics.
Occupancy — A CUDA resource and scheduling metric describing active warps relative to architectural limits; it is not a direct measure of useful throughput.
Pinned memory — Host memory arranged to support direct asynchronous transfer behavior required by particular CUDA workflows.
Real-time system — A system whose correctness includes timing requirements in addition to logical results.
SIMT — Single instruction, multiple threads; CUDA's execution model in which threads are grouped for hardware execution while retaining thread-level semantics.
Stream — A CUDA ordering domain for asynchronous operations.
Throughput — Completed work per unit time under a stated workload.
Warp — The hardware execution grouping used by NVIDIA GPUs for CUDA threads.
